seo.title: Contract review
seo.seo_description: Contract review: a WorkStudio starter template for small business. Starting fields, steps, human approval and what is left to validate with your adviser.

blocks.role: Promesse de la fiche : ce que fait le gabarit « Revue de contrat », dit sans détour.

translation.headline: Contract review.
translation.subheadline: The Contract review template flags risky clauses (a table with quoted extract and level), common missing clauses and questions to ask, according to your role and priorities.

blocks.role: Réponse d'abord : ce que fait le gabarit, en trois lignes.

translation.title: The short answer.
translation.body:
The Contract review template flags risky clauses (a table with quoted extract and level), common missing clauses and questions to ask, according to your role and priorities. A person approves the review; only their approval emails the summary, noting that it is not legal advice.

A workflow template is an automated sequence of tasks, provided as a starting point in WorkStudio and to be adapted to the business before it is deployed.

blocks.role: Les champs de départ du gabarit, tels que déclarés dans WorkStudio.

translation.title: What you provide.
translation.body:
Each starting field is pre-filled with an example value so a first run needs no typing, except email addresses and files.

  • The contract. Text of the contract or clauses to review.
  • The context. Your role in the contract and your priorities.
  • The recipient. Email address to send the summary to.

blocks.role: Les étapes du flux : ce que fait chaque agent, où une personne intervient.

cards.title: Carry out the review.
cards.text: An agent presents risky clauses (article, quoted extract, risk, level), common missing clauses (confidentiality, reversibility, protection of personal information, liability cap, governing law) and questions, citing nothing but the text provided.

cards.title: Get approval.
cards.text: A person reads the review and approves or refuses it.

cards.title: Send the summary.
cards.text: If approved, the summary goes by email, subject "Revue de contrat (ne constitue pas un avis juridique)".

blocks.role: Ce qui s'adapte avant l'usage : le propre du gabarit, le commun, l'envoi.

cards.title: What to adapt here.
cards.text: The review cites only what is in the text. The "common" clauses come from an AI model, not from a Quebec lawyer: have the contract reviewed by a lawyer.

cards.title: What applies to all.
cards.text: The templates are written for a Quebec small business: amounts in Canadian dollars, GST and QST wherever a tax applies, and Quebec business vocabulary. They do not guarantee any tax or legal compliance: the examples are fictional, and your accountant or adviser validates the result before use.

cards.title: A person approves before sending.
cards.text: The flow stops for a person's approval and sends the email only if they approve. The mail server (host, port, account, sender) is left to fill in.

blocks.role: Questions de la fiche : envoi, point propre au gabarit, adaptation au Québec.

items.question: Can it send an email without my approval?
items.answer: No. The flow stops for a person's approval and sends the email only if they approve. The mail server must be filled in.

items.question: Who receives the summary?
items.answer: The email address you give in the starting field, and only after a person approves.

items.question: Is it suited to a Quebec business?
items.answer: It is written for Quebec but still needs validating: the examples are fictional, and the template does not replace your accountant or adviser. Review every result before using it and adapt the instructions to your business.

blocks.role: Appel à l'action : démonstration sur données fictives.

translation.title: See it at work.
translation.text: A demonstration on fictional data, to see what the template prepares and where a person stays in control.
